name: Speaking Up Drill — Raising a Concern With a Senior
_note: Skill drill. Standard 4 metric keys re-pitched: medical_accuracy = clarity of the concern stated, clinical_reasoning slot = graded assertiveness & advocacy (the focus), communication_fluency = composure with a senior.

anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; meaning always clear

anchors.90-100: States the specific safety concern and the reason unmistakably
anchors.70-80: Concern is clear with only minor vagueness
anchors.50-60: Concern is raised but somewhat unclear or buried
anchors.30-40: Hints at a worry but never states it plainly

anchors.90-100: Escalates appropriately (concern → discomfort → safety) and advocates firmly yet respectfully
anchors.70-80: Raises and holds the concern respectfully
anchors.50-60: Raises it but backs down too easily under pushback
anchors.10-20: Stays silent / simply complies; no advocacy

anchors.90-100: Calm, fluent, and professional despite the hierarchy and time pressure
anchors.50-60: Noticeably nervous but gets the message across
anchors.30-40: Flustered or over-apologetic to the point of muddling the message

anchors.90-100: Challenges the plan while staying respectful and collaborative — never aggressive or undermining
anchors.50-60: Mostly respectful; slightly blunt or overly deferential
anchors.30-40: Either confrontational or so deferential the patient is left unprotected
anchors.10-20: Rude/insubordinate, or abandons the patient's interest entirely

checklist.item: raised the concern rather than silently complying
stated the specific reason / safety issue clearly
used graded, respectful assertiveness (not aggressive, not over-apologetic)
held the concern when the senior pushed back
kept the exchange collaborative and professional
